chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Yazid al-Kunasi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Your son is more entitled with respect to you than your grandson; and your grandson is more entitled with respect to you than your brother. And your full brother (from your father and mother) is more entitled with respect to you than your paternal half-brother. And your paternal half-brother is more entitled with respect to you than your maternal half-brother. And the son of your full brother is more entitled with respect to you than the son of your paternal half-brother. And the son of your paternal half-brother is more entitled with respect to you than your paternal uncle. And your paternal uncle who is a full brother of your father (from both his father and mother) is more entitled with respect to you than your paternal uncle who is a paternal half-brother of your father. And your paternal uncle who is a paternal half-brother of your father is more entitled with respect to you than your paternal uncle who is a maternal half-brother of your father. And the son of your paternal uncle who is a full brother of your father is more entitled with respect to you than the son of your paternal uncle who is a paternal half-brother of your father. And the son of your paternal uncle who is a paternal half-brother of your father is more entitled with respect to you than the son of your paternal uncle who is a maternal half-brother of your father.

key_terms.أَوْلَى: More entitled/prior in right — a technical term in inheritance jurisprudence indicating priority of claim
key_terms.ابن: Son — in inheritance law, male lineal descendants take priority by degree
key_terms.عَمّ: Paternal uncle (father's brother) — relevant in the third class of Quranic heirs

ai.seo_question: What is the order of inheritance priority among relatives according to Imam al-Baqir in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) enumerates the precise hierarchical order of inheritance priority among relatives. The hadith establishes that closer blood ties and stronger kinship bonds confer priority in inheritance: sons over grandsons, grandsons over brothers, full siblings over half-siblings by paternity, paternal half-siblings over maternal half-siblings. This systematic ordering reflects the Shia jurisprudential framework for calculating inheritance shares (mirath), where degree of kinship and parental connection determine priority of claim.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhahhad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Yazeed Al Kunasy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Your son is more entitled with you than the son of your son (grandson); and a son of your son (grandson) is more entitled with you than your brother. And your brother from your father and your mother (full brother) is more entitled with you than your brother from your father (only – half brother). And your brother from your father (paternal half brother) is more entitled with you than your brother from your mother (maternal half brother). 
And a son of your brother from your father and your mother (son of a full brother) is more entitled with you that the son of your brother from your father (only – son of half brother). And a son of your brother from your father (son of half brother) is more entitled with you than your paternal uncle. And your paternal uncle, a brother of your father from your father and your mother is more entitled with you than your paternal uncle, a brother of your father from his father.
And you paternal uncle, a brother of your father, from his father is more entitled with you than your maternal uncle, a brother of your father from his mother. And a son of your paternal uncle, a brother of your father from his father and his mother, is more entitled with you than a son of your paternal uncle, a brother of your father from his father. And a son of your paternal uncle, a brother of your father from his father is more entitled with you than a son of your paternal uncle, a brother of your father, from his mother’.
